analysis.title: GS Kaplan - A few observations from today 22 Oct 2026
key_insights: As of midday, GS PB had Fundamental L/S down 1.1%, Systematics down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4%. This is the first time since Covid that all three strategies were down more than 1% on the same day.
The HF Positioning Pair (GSTHVIPP) finished down about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and is down 10.4% month to date.
US 10YR yields finished lower by about 15bps, the largest one-day move since August 2025, as the AI-driven selloff forces investors to reassess longer-term growth expectations.

The correlation between NDX and US 10YR yields continues to stand out. The 10YR closed below the CTA short-term threshold, which GS expects to bring more bond demand in tomorrow morning's flow estimates.
GS is watching for continued spillover or flight to quality driven by European rates overnight.

The bull case for the week was that tech earnings would stabilize the tape. Reactions were constructive on Wednesday, but META and LRCX failed to continue that theme on Thursday. WDC is up 2% after hours ahead of a busy week of Megacap earnings.
The GS AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% from its June highs, a similar drawdown to the one before the bounce in July.
High Beta Momentum (GSPRHIMO) has erased all of its YTD gains, driven by the AI-correlated long leg. Historically, similar momentum drawdowns have been attractive entry points.
SPX ex. AI (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P by 6% month to date and is closing its performance gap. 45% of SPX names have negative beta with the index.

Flows on the GS desk showed no sign of offense around the AI theme. Unlike last week, there was little rotation out of AI into defensives, despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and pockets of Financials.

The GS floor finished 9.6% better for sale. Asset Managers were about 20% better for sale on supply in large cap tech and ETFs. Hedge Funds were 10% better for sale on supply in semis and hardware, with ETF shorting up (shorts outpacing long sales by 2:1).

Dispersion was extreme: 155 S&P names had moves of 2.0 sigma or more, the highest since the May 2025 US-China tariff truce, while 335 names in the S&P finished higher. This is one of the widest spreads between S&P breadth and index performance since the 1990s.
earnings_insights: META and LRCX reactions on 10/22 failed to continue Wednesday's constructive earnings reactions (reported reactions, no figures given).
WDC reported 10/22 after the close and was up 2% after hours.
A busy week of Megacap earnings follows.

Historically, similar momentum drawdowns have been attractive entry points and the AI basket is at a drawdown similar to the one before the July bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: META and LRCX failed to continue the constructive earnings theme on Thursday. There were no signs of offense around AI on the GS desk, with hedge funds and asset managers better for sale in tech and semis.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Megacap earnings next week failing to extend the constructive reaction, with WDC (up 2% after hours) as the next test.
